Note: The diagram uses (min, max) cardinality notation where:
- (1,1) indicates one-to-one relationship (each entity participates exactly once)
- (1,N) or (1,*) indicates one-to-many relationship (one entity can relate to many)
- (0,1) indicates optional participation (zero or one)
- (0,N) or (0,*) indicates optional many participation (zero or many)


A university database system is designed to manage information about faculty members, courses, students, and departments. The Faculty entity has attributes: FacultyID, Name, and Email. The Course entity includes CourseID, Title, and Credits. The Student entity has attributes such as StudentID, Name, Email. contains StudentID, Name, and EnrollmentDate. The Department entity has attributes such as DepartmentID, DepartmentName, Location. consists of DepartmentID, Name, and Budget. Faculty members may teach multiple courses, and courses can have many students enrolled. Each course belongs to one department. There is a specialization where some faculty can be 'Adjunct Faculty' with an additional attribute: ContractEndDate, and some students can be 'Graduate Students' with an additional attribute: ThesisTitle. A Faculty can be related to many Courses through the 'Teaches' relationship (Faculty participation is optional). A Student can be related to many Courses, and a Course can be related to many Students through the 'EnrolledIn' relationship (Student participation is optional, Course participation is optional). Many Courses can be related to one Department through the 'BelongsTo' relationship (Department participation is optional)

questions.text: Consider the following schema of a database designed for a Library: Book (bookId: int, title: varchar(100), author: varchar(50), publicationYear: int) Member (memberId: int, name: varchar(100), email: varchar(50), phone: varchar(15)) Loan (loanId: int, bookId: int, memberId: int, loanDate: date, returnDate: date) Fine (fineId: int, memberId: int, amount: real, paymentStatus: varchar(20)). The 'Book' table stores information about books available in the library, including unique book ID, title, author, and publication year. The 'Member' table keeps details of library members, containing their ID, name, email, and phone number. The 'Loan' table records transactions between members and books, with information on loan IDs, book IDs, member IDs, loan dates, and return dates. The 'Fine' table tracks fines incurred by members, providing details such as fine IDs, member IDs, fine amounts, and payment statuses. The 'Member' table holds details about library members, such as their unique member ID, first name, last name, email, phone number, and address. The 'Loan' table manages book loans, with each loan having a unique ID and being associated with a specific book and member. It records the loan date, due date, and return date. The 'Fine' table contains information about fines incurred by members for late returns or other penalties. It includes a fine ID, member ID, fine amount, and payment status.
